messages:
Anne: Heads-up — the console is showing a bunch of requests attributed to 'projectless' for org-redwood, but the service keys are definitely bound to project:analytics. Can someone check routing/attribution?
Sam: hmm, that sounds like the fallback routing path. Did you see quota hits or just billing attribution? :thinking_face:
Anne: mainly billing attribution noise and a spike in the rateband dashboard. quota counters still look fine.
Lee: what region/edge was this from? could be a proxy that strips the origin header and triggers the projectless fallback.
Anne: us-west-2. I grabbed a quick query from request logs:
```
select count(*) as c, origin_project, routing_path
from requests
where org = 'org-redwood' and ts >= now()-1h
group by origin_project, routing_path
order by c desc
limit 50
```
Sam: nice. if routing_path == "fallback:projectless" then our router may have dropped the claim. Can you paste a sample request id?
Anne: 7f3b2c1e-9a4 — looking at headers it has `x-origin-project: analytics` earlier in the chain but the auth-proxy shows empty project claim.
Mike: maybe token exchange step is timing out and we fall back to service-account origin? we've seen a similar pattern with ephemeral exchanges.
Cory: quick theory: token introspection service returned 500 for a subset so router used the conservative path and matched org-only key -> projectless. Telemetry didn't mark the error as routed, so dashboards only show projectless counts.
Tia: that would explain the rateband jump — projectless counts are grouped into the org fallback bucket which has a different rateband. Do we have traces for that request id?
Sam: asking tracing infra — @deploy-bot can you pull span for 7f3b2c1e-9a4?
deploy-bot: fetching spans for trace 7f3b2c1e-9a4...  (takes ~12s)
deploy-bot: found trace across auth-proxy -> token-introspect -> router -> serving. token-introspect returned 500 at 1718899067.
Lee: confirms Cory's theory. token-introspect 500 -> router used org-only fallback. Needs a mitigation: either make router preserve origin header when introspection fails, or surface a telemetry tag so console can highlight "introspection failures" in attribution views.
Anne: I prefer both: short-term telemetry flag, longer-term router fix. For telemetry, we can add `attribution_reason` tag with values: ok|introspect-error|missing-claim|expired-token. Then dashboards can filter.
Mike: agree. also we should avoid silently changing rateband on fallback. Can we map fallback attribution to retain project-level rateband until explicit deny?
Cory: risky — if we keep project rateband we could undercharge when claims are missing. Better to show a split: keep project attribution when header present but mark as "soft-attributed" until introspect confirms.
Tia: UX note: console should show a hover explaining soft-attributed vs authoritative attribution. Product asked for clear call-to-action: "pin this project's attribution" for customers who want to override fallback while we fix infra.
Sam: implementation plan proposal:
- short-term (1d): add `attribution_reason` telemetry and a new console filter + tooltip. (owner: Anne)
- mid-term (1w): router change to add `soft_attribution=true` when header exists but introspect fails, and expose toggle to prefer soft. (owner: Lee)
- long-term (2-3w): harden introspect paths, retry circuit, instrument SLOs. (owner: Mike)
Anne: I'll file a quick RFC and create the dashboard filter. Sam, can you own updating the telemetry schema?
Sam: yes. I'll add the tag to the request events and update the log-parsing job.
Cory: I'll open a console UX PR for the tooltip + pin action.
Tia: I'll draft the copy for the hover and the support KB entry.
Anne: great. one more ask — can we add an alert when introspect 5xx rate > 0.5% in last 5m? we missed this earlier.
Mike: yep, alerting on introspect error rate makes sense. I'll add to ops playbook and put a runbook link in the alert.
Sam: created telemetry ticket (#ENG-1412). Anne: created dashboard filter and provisional chart. Cory: console PR in draft.
Anne: thanks team :thumbsup: I'll update the RFC with owners and timelines.
Tia: nice triage. happy to help with KB once PR is merged.
Sam: closing loop: any objections to the short-term telemetry name `attribution_reason`?
Cory: fine by me.
Mike: good.
Anne: 👍
